title: HoneyBook: client relationship platform for small businesses
supports: Lead forms that capture inquiries, a pipeline from inquiry to project milestones, proposals, contracts and invoices sent together with online payments, a scheduler, automations, questionnaires and a client portal, AI email drafts and a meeting notetaker; aimed at photographers, venues, event planners, designers and home and real estate professionals; available in the US, Canada, UK and Australia. Vendor homepage. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Tripleseat: event management software for restaurants, hotels and venues
supports: Captures and routes event inquiries (Inquiry Inbox), proposals, contracts and BEOs, payments, floor plans, a guest portal and a venue marketplace; vendor claims use by more than 20,000 venues and operation since 2008. Vendor homepage. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Use Google Workspace connectors
supports: Claude's Gmail connector can search, read, draft, send, reply and forward; by default Claude asks for approval before each of these actions, and Team and Enterprise owners decide whether members may skip that; the Calendar connector can create and update events and find availability; owners must enable connectors on Team and Enterprise plans. Page marked 'Updated this week'. Opened with WebFetch.

title: HubSpot MCP server
supports: HubSpot publishes a remote MCP server for CRM access and a local developer MCP server; the page lists read and write access to contacts, companies, deals, tickets, products, orders, line items, invoices, quotes and engagements, while its FAQ mentions read-only access to standard records; connection by OAuth with an admin connecting first. Opened with WebFetch.

title: State of Sales Report
supports: Nine in ten sales teams use AI agents or expect to within two years; teams deploy agents across the sales process from planning to quoting. Vendor survey page with no stated edition, sample or date. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Deduplication of records
supports: Contacts are deduplicated by email and companies by primary domain; imports update matching records and rows with no unique identifier import as new records; companies created through the API are not deduplicated by domain; up to ten custom properties per object can require unique values; Record ID can match records on import. Last updated 2 October 2026. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Set up and customize pipelines
supports: Separate pipelines are recommended only when processes have different stages; each deal stage carries a probability used for weighted amounts; reporting needs both Won and Lost stages; conditional stage rules can make properties required before a record is created in or moved to a stage; custom pipelines need Starter or above. Last updated 29 September 2026. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Principles of the GDPR
supports: Personal data must be accurate and kept up to date, and corrected or deleted without delay when wrong; it must be stored for the shortest time possible, and organisations should set time limits to erase or review it. Undated page. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Use legacy quotes
supports: The legacy quotes tool is no longer available to new users; a default expiration period can be set; optional approvals require quotes to be approved before they reach the buyer (Sales Hub Enterprise); e-signatures draw on a pooled monthly limit; a setting lets buyers pay quotes before signing; published quotes do not update when branding changes. Last updated 24 September 2026. Opened with WebFetch.

title: QuickBooks Online pricing
supports: QuickBooks lists a Free plan plus Simple Start, Essentials, Plus and Advanced, with a 30-day free trial; the Free plan's invoicing lets users see estimate status and convert estimates into invoices. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Xero pricing plans (US)
supports: Xero has no free plan; its Early, Growing and Established plans all include sending quotes. Opened with WebFetch.

title: 15 U.S. Code 7001: General rule of validity (ESIGN Act)
publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
supports: A signature, contract or record in interstate or foreign commerce may not be denied legal effect solely because it is electronic; where a law requires written information to a consumer, electronic delivery needs the consumer's affirmative consent after set disclosures. Statute text. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Providing clear and accurate information about prices: summary (CMA209)
supports: Invitations to purchase must show the total price; mandatory fees and charges should normally be in the headline total and showing them separately will not normally be enough; drip pricing is prohibited, with fines up to 10% of turnover or GBP 300,000, whichever is greater; 'from' prices must include mandatory charges such as a flat booking fee (photography example); local charges such as resort fees are included, with pay-now and pay-locally amounts beside the total; where the total depends on the customer's needs, give what is needed to work it out. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Price transparency (CMA209)
supports: CMA guidance on price transparency under the unfair commercial practices law, covering mandatory fees, drip pricing and partitioned pricing; published 18 November 2025, summary added 7 January 2026. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Unfair commercial practices (CMA207)
supports: CMA guidance on business-to-consumer conduct prohibited under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024; published 4 April 2025, updated 18 November 2025. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees: Frequently Asked Questions
supports: Effective 12 May 2025; covers live-event tickets and short-term lodging (hotels, motels, inns, vacation rentals), including third-party sellers and travel agents, and protects business as well as individual buyers; any price shown must disclose the total including known mandatory fees, more prominently than other pricing; only government charges, shipping and optional add-ons may be left out, disclosed before payment; fee names must be truthful. Page dated May 2025. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Returns and cancellations (right of withdrawal)
supports: EU consumers can cancel distance and off-premises contracts within 14 days without a reason; for services the period runs from the day the contract is agreed; exceptions include plane and train tickets, concert tickets, hotel bookings, car rental and catering services for specific dates, made-to-order goods and services fully delivered after the customer agreed to start. Last checked 28 April 2026. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Online and distance selling for businesses
supports: UK businesses must tell customers they can cancel within 14 days; if not told, customers can cancel for up to 12 months more; listed exemptions include goods and services of GBP 42 or less, package holidays and passenger travel tickets; information required before an order includes business details, full price with taxes, payment and cancellation terms and deposit conditions, given on paper or in a form the customer can keep, plus a copy of the contract. Undated page. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Package travel
supports: A package combines two or more types of travel service for the same trip under one contract or in linked ways (one point of sale, inclusive price, advertised as a package, linked online booking within 24 hours); information required before booking includes the total price, payment terms and passport and visa requirements, plus a standard EU form; price rises only for specific costs, if the contract allows, and not later than 20 days before the trip; over 8% the traveller may end the contract without a fee; insolvency protection applies. Last checked 11 May 2026. Opened with WebFetch.

title: What does ATOL protection mean?
supports: ATOL is financial protection, not insurance, for package trips that include a flight and for flights sold as ATOL protected; the customer should receive an ATOL Certificate naming the ATOL holder, including when booking through a travel agent. Undated page. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Estate Agency Team
supports: The team enforces the Estate Agents Act 1979 and the Tenant Fees Act 2019; it published an opinion on 5 May 2022 that 'price on application' property listings were unlawful, and a statement on conditional selling on 15 July 2025. Opened with WebFetch.

title: National Trading Standards publishes guidance on Part A material information for property listings
supports: Part A material information for all property listings: price or rent, council tax band (rates in Northern Ireland) and, for sales, tenure; Rightmove, Zoopla, OnTheMarket and PropertyPal added fields and flag listings that leave them empty; published 12 July 2022; Parts B and C to cover utilities and other matters. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Material information
supports: Notes that the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government announced in June 2026 its intention to introduce homebuying sales packs as part of wider reforms. Opened with WebFetch.

title: The Fair Housing Act
publisher: US Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division
supports: The Fair Housing Act bars discrimination by housing providers including real estate companies, covering steering and misleading information about availability; protected characteristics are race or color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status and disability. Updated 22 June 2023. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Highlights from the Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers
supports: 2026 edition covering US transactions from July 2025 to June 2026: 92% of sellers used an agent; 22% of buyers were first-time buyers; published yearly since 1981. Trade body survey. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Incoterms rules
supports: Incoterms 2020 is the current edition, in force since 1 January 2020, with eleven three-letter trade terms that set out the tasks, costs and risks of delivering goods from seller to buyer; first published 1936. Opened with WebFetch.

title: X12 transaction sets
supports: Standard EDI documents: 850 Purchase Order, 855 Purchase Order Acknowledgment, 856 Ship Notice/Manifest, 860 Purchase Order Change Request (buyer initiated), 865 Purchase Order Change Acknowledgment/Request (seller initiated) and 810 Invoice. Opened with WebFetch.
